name: Moses and the uncircumcised son
charge: Neglecting the sign of the covenant in his own house
summary: Sent back to Egypt with the rod of God in his hand, Moses took his wife and his sons and went. He had just been given the message for Pharaoh: Israel is my son, even my firstborn; let my son go, and if thou refuse, I will slay thy son, even thy firstborn. By the way in the inn the Lord met him and sought to kill him, because his own son was uncircumcised. Zipporah took a sharp stone and circumcised the child and cast the foreskin at his feet, and said, Surely a bloody husband art thou to me. So he let him go.
offense: Circumcision was not a Sinai ordinance. It was given to Abraham centuries earlier as the token of the covenant, every man child among you shall be circumcised, and he that is eight days old shall be circumcised among you, every man child in your generations (Genesis 17:10-12), with the penalty written into it: the uncircumcised man child whose flesh of his foreskin is not circumcised, that soul shall be cut off from his people, he hath broken my covenant (Genesis 17:14). That is why the deliverer of Israel was worthy of death on the road, and it is why the case belongs in this volume as evidence that the law was in force long before it was written in stone. Two things sharpen it. Egypt did not practise it, and Israel was afterwards told plainly, after the doings of the land of Egypt, wherein ye dwelt, shall ye not do (Leviticus 18:3), so a man raised in Pharaoh's house had taken up the omission of the country he was raised in. And the errand he was carrying makes it intolerable: he had just been given the words, Israel is my son, even my firstborn; let  my son go, and if thou refuse, I will slay thy son, even thy firstborn (Exodus 4:22-23). He was going to demand another man's firstborn on pain of death while his own son bore no token of the covenant he was invoking.
judgment: The Lord met him and sought to kill him (Exodus 4:24), which is the sentence of Genesis 17:14 falling on the head of the house rather than on the child. The remedy was immediate and it was performed by his wife: then Zipporah took a sharp stone, and cut off the foreskin of her son, and cast it at his feet, and said, Surely a bloody husband art thou to me (Exodus 4:25). So he let him go; then she said, A bloody husband thou art, because of the circumcision (Exodus 4:26), and the record explains her own words so that they are not mistaken for a complaint about anything else. The record gives no further comment, and the placing is the comment: the thing had to be set right in his own house before he could carry a word from God into Pharaoh's. The same neglect cost the next generation as well, for all the people born in the wilderness had not been circumcised, and Joshua had to make sharp knives and circumcise them again the second time before they took the land (Joshua 5:2-5). The token was never withdrawn: Abraham was ninety years old and nine when he was circumcised  (Genesis 17:24), and Paul took and circumcised Timothy because of the Jews which were in those quarters (Acts 16:3). Circumcision verily profiteth, if thou keep the law (Romans 2:25), and the circumcision of the heart is commanded alongside it and not instead of it, circumcise yourselves to the Lord, and take away the foreskins of your heart (Jeremiah 4:4).

verses.text: And it came to pass by the way in the inn, that the Lord met him, and sought to kill him.
Then Zipporah took a sharp stone, and cut off the foreskin of her son, and cast it at his feet, and said, Surely a bloody husband art thou to me.
So he let him go: then she said, A bloody husband thou art, because of the circumcision.
This is my covenant, which ye shall keep, between me and you and thy seed after thee; Every man child among you shall be circumcised.
And ye shall circumcise the flesh of your foreskin; and it shall be a token of the covenant betwixt me and you.
And he that is eight days old shall be circumcised among you, every man child in your generations, he that is born in the house, or bought with money of any stranger, which is not of thy seed.
He that is born in thy house, and he that is bought with thy money, must needs be circumcised: and my covenant shall be in your flesh for an everlasting covenant.
And the uncircumcised man child whose flesh of his foreskin is not circumcised, that soul shall be cut off from his people; he hath broken my covenant.
At that time the Lord said unto Joshua, Make thee sharp knives, and circumcise again the children of Israel the second time.
And Joshua made him sharp knives, and circumcised the children of Israel at the hill of the foreskins.
And this is the cause why Joshua did circumcise: All the people that came out of Egypt, that were males, even all the men of war, died in the wilderness by the way, after they came out of Egypt.
Now all the people that came out were circumcised: but all the people that were born in the wilderness by the way as they came forth out of Egypt, them they had not circumcised.

entries.commentary: Moses answered, But, behold, they will not believe me, nor hearken unto my voice. Moses knew the spirit of his people: Israel is impudent, hardhearted, and stiffnecked, a rebellious house that does not like to listen even when shown precept upon precept. The word to Ezekiel is the same commission: Israel is not a people of a strange speech and hard language; had the prophet been sent to such, they would have hearkened; but the house of Israel will not hearken. Go, get thee to them of the captivity, and speak unto them, whether they will hear or whether they will forbear. That stubbornness is itself a mark of who the Israelites are among the nations today.

The first sign: the rod cast on the ground became a serpent, and Moses fled from before it; he caught it by the tail and it became a rod in his hand. The sign was given that they may believe that the LORD God of their fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, hath appeared unto thee. Israel would not believe on a man's word alone; it took a miracle, because we were a people of little faith.

The second sign: Moses put his hand into his bosom, and when he took it out, his hand was leprous as snow; he put it in again, and it was turned again as his other flesh. This was a miracle precisely because Moses was a very dark-skinned man; the daughters of the priest of Midian had taken him for an Egyptian. The hand came out white as snow and went back to his natural dark skin; had he been white already there would have been no sign in it. If they will not believe the first sign, they will believe the voice of the latter sign; the magicians of Egypt could imitate serpents, but not this.
The third sign: if they will not believe the first two, take of the water of the river and pour it upon the dry land, and the water shall become blood upon the dry land.

Moses said, O my Lord, I am not eloquent, but I am slow of speech, and of a slow tongue. Moses did not stutter, as is commonly taught; he was not fluent in the Hebrew tongue. He was learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians and mighty in words and in deeds, but he grew up in Pharaoh's house speaking the Egyptian language and then spent forty years in Midian, and a language moves on in forty years. The LORD answered, Who hath made man's mouth? Now therefore go, and I will be with thy mouth, and teach thee what thou shalt say.

Moses pressed, Send, I pray thee, by the hand of him whom thou wilt send; and the anger of the LORD was kindled against Moses. Is not Aaron the Levite thy brother? I know that he can speak well; he spoke the Hebrew of the people fluently. Aaron shall be thy spokesman unto the people: he shall be to thee instead of a mouth, and thou shalt be to him instead of God. Moses stood as God in this instance, speaking through Aaron his prophet, who interpreted to the people. And thou shalt take this rod in thine hand, wherewith thou shalt do signs.

Moses returned to Jethro his father in law and asked leave, and Jethro said, Go in peace. The LORD said, Go, return into Egypt: for all the men are dead which sought thy life; the Pharaoh of chapter 2 had died. Moses took his wife and his sons and returned to the land of Egypt, and Moses took the rod of God in his hand. The LORD told him, Do all those wonders before Pharaoh which I have put in thine hand: but I will harden his heart, that he shall not let the people go. Thou shalt say unto Pharaoh, Thus saith the LORD, Israel is my son, even my firstborn. Israel was not the first nation created; it was among the last. But Israel is the first nation the Most High chose, the apple of His eye from Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob down. If thou refuse to let him go, behold, I will slay thy son, even thy firstborn.

By the way in the inn, the LORD met him, and sought to kill him, because Moses had not circumcised his son. Zipporah took a sharp stone, cut off the foreskin of her son, and said, Surely a bloody husband art thou to me: bloody because of the circumcision she had to perform herself. This shows the laws did not begin at Sinai. Circumcision was the covenant given to Abraham for every man child in his generations, on the eighth day, and the uncircumcised man child whose flesh is not circumcised, that soul shall be cut off from his people: he hath broken my covenant. That is why Moses was worthy of death.

The LORD sent Aaron into the wilderness to meet Moses, and he met him in the mount of God and kissed him; Aaron believed right away. Moses told Aaron all the words of the LORD and all the signs. Aaron spake all the words which the LORD had spoken unto Moses and did the signs in the sight of the people, and the people believed: and when they heard that the LORD had visited the children of Israel, and that he had looked upon their affliction, they bowed their heads and worshipped. After a long time in which the Lord had not been dealing with them, He finally heard their prayers.

At ninety and nine years old Abram was commanded to walk before the Most High and be perfect. There is no age excuse; Christ said nothing new in [Matthew 5:48](/bible/matthew/5#v48), for the command to be perfect was given thousands of years before. Perfect according to the scriptures means to walk in His statutes and keep His commandments; that is how Israel perfects itself.

When the Most High began dealing with Abram on a covenant level, his name was changed: Abram became Abraham, a father of many nations, and kings would come out of him. Father of many nations does not mean everybody is spiritually a child of Abraham. The same promise was passed down the seed line: Jacob's name was changed to Israel and told a nation and a company of nations and kings would come out of his loins. The blessing of all men and the covenant were made to rest upon the head of Jacob and divided among the twelve tribes. Kings come out of that seed, including Christ, the King of kings.
The covenant is with Abraham's seed after him, and seed is literal offspring, not a spiritual metaphor. The Most High promised to be a God to Abraham and to his seed after him.

Circumcision is the token of the covenant: every man child circumcised at eight days, and the uncircumcised soul cut off from his people. Abraham received circumcision as a seal of the righteousness of the faith he had yet being uncircumcised. He believed and obeyed first, and circumcision sealed it; likewise a brother can come into the truth, get built up in the faith, and then go through with the process. It still has to be done. A covenant is a contract with terms; the covenant was confirmed to Jacob for a law, and circumcision is one of the laws within the covenant.

Sarai's name was changed to Sarah, and she shall be a mother of nations; those are the same nations of the covenant, and she and Abraham had one child together, Isaac. Abraham fell on his face and laughed in his heart: shall a child be born to a hundred year old man, and Sarah bear at ninety? The Most High read his thought and named the child from it: Isaac means he will laugh.

Ishmael received a blessing: fruitful, multiplied exceedingly, twelve princes, a great nation. But the word to Abraham was kings shall come out of thee, and the covenant passes to Isaac: my covenant will I establish with Isaac. Not all who are of Abraham's seed are the children; in Isaac shall thy seed be called. Ishmael was born of the flesh, of Sarai's plan, with no word from God ordaining it; the children of the promise are counted for the seed.

The selfsame day Abraham circumcised every male of his house, himself at ninety and nine and Ishmael at thirteen. That is the righteous example: he received the commandment and performed it the same day.

The kings of the Amorites and the Canaanites heard that the Lord had dried up the waters of Jordan from before the children of Israel, and their heart melted: they were paralyzed with fear. They had heard how the Most High split the Red sea in Exodus, and now he had done it again at Jordan, so neither was there spirit in them any more because of the children of Israel.

Circumcise again the children of Israel the second time: the children of Israel had not been keeping the commandments, being stiffnecked and hardheaded, and the Lord told Joshua to fix them. Circumcision is the covenant the Most High instituted with our forefather Abraham: every man child circumcised at eight days old, and the servant born in the house or bought with money circumcised likewise and keeping the laws as well. When Abraham received the commandment he performed it, circumcising every male of his house the selfsame day; he showed the Lord by his actions that he believed. So the men in Joshua who had not been circumcised showed a form of repentance by applying the law of circumcision.

This is the cause of the circumcision: all the men of war that came out of Egypt died in the wilderness because they obeyed not the voice of the Lord, and the generation born by the way had not been circumcised. That they had not circumcised themselves means they did not obey the voice of the Lord: they should have been circumcised physically and also mentally and spiritually. The land that floweth with milk and honey is understood by the Bible's own dictionary, precept upon precept: the rebels in Numbers called Egypt the land flowing with milk and honey, and Israel was brought out of the land of Egypt, so the phrase describes a land abundant in food. The milk goes into your cattle and your meats, and the honey goes into your vegetation. The mixed multitude and the children of Israel wept for the fish, cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions, and garlic they ate in Egypt: they were comfortable in their oppression and did not understand they were not free, the same mindset among our people in captivity today who say they are free and living their best life. The honey teaching carries a dietary lesson: hast thou found honey, eat so much as is sufficient for thee. Do not overeat; balance your salts, sugars, meats, and dainties moderately.

Their children raised up in their stead Joshua circumcised, for they had not circumcised them by the way. A father can have his son circumcised in the flesh yet never circumcise him from the heart: if he never teaches him the laws and to obey the voice of the Lord, the physical circumcision alone profits him nothing. It is symbolic of obeying the voice of the Lord.
They abode in their places in the camp till they were whole: these were grown men, not eight day old babies, so they had to remain in the camp until they healed from the circumcision.

This day have I rolled away the reproach of Egypt from off you: they finally believed and obeyed, circumcising themselves and obeying the voice of the Lord, so they were no longer a reproach, an embarrassment, or a disgrace. The children of Israel finally sanctified themselves, and the name of the place is called Gilgal unto this day.

The children of Israel encamped in Gilgal and kept the passover on the fourteenth day of the month at even in the plains of Jericho; the passover was instituted by the Most High, and you can read about it in [Exodus 12](/bible/exodus/12). They did eat of the old corn of the land on the morrow after the passover, and the manna ceased; the children of Israel had manna no more, but ate of the fruit of the land of Canaan that year.

Joshua lifted up his eyes by Jericho and saw a man standing over against him with his sword drawn, a warrior. Joshua did not run; he went straight to him and asked, Art thou for us, or for our adversaries? There was no fear in the heart of Joshua. The man answered, Nay; but as captain of the host of the Lord am I now come. Host means army: he is the captain, the leader, of the army of the Lord. When Joshua realized who stood before him, the fear came: he fell on his face to the earth and did worship, and the leader of Israel's army called himself a servant, saying, What saith my lord unto his servant? Joshua had cleaved to Moses and understood who the captain of the host is. The captain of the host of the Lord is Christ, the captain of our salvation. This is why Joshua was afraid: the return of Christ is not the soft picture Christianity paints, for he is not coming back made like unto his brethren as at the first, but with the power of the living God, to take vengeance and destroy. No missiles or fighter jets will do anything against him.
The captain of the Lord's host said, Loose thy shoe from off thy foot; for the place whereon thou standest is holy. And Joshua did so.
